source.title: Optimal generalisation and learning transition in extensive-width shallow neural networks near interpolation
source.authors: Jean Barbier; Francesco Camilli; Minh-Toan Nguyen; Mauro Pastore; Rudy Skerk

record.tranche_reason: The study varies sample rate and reports generalisation error near the parameter-count scale, but uses a Bayes-optimal teacher-student analysis and experiments rather than a model-size sweep.
record.gate_note: The reported generalisation-error curves against sample rate and the test-loss trajectories during ADAM training bear on V3 and V2, respectively. The paper also reports learning-transition locations, overlaps, mutual information, and training time to reach thresholds; those do not themselves measure the error shapes in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study computes Bayes-optimal generalisation error against sample rate α = n/d² for a two-layer network, across the interpolation threshold n ≈ kd (α = γ = 0.5). It checks this with MCMC/HMC and GAMP-RIE. That bears on V3 in a new setting: Bayes-optimal inference rather than unregularised training. The paper never frames its results as double descent.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors derive an effective replica theory for Bayes-optimal error in extensive-width two-layer networks with n ∝ d². They find a universal phase, with slow error decay independent of the weight prior, and a specialisation phase, with faster, prior-dependent decay, separated by a discontinuous transition. For Gaussian weights this transition requires activation terms beyond Hermite degree 2. The specialisation solution may be algorithmically hard to find, while GAMP-RIE reaches the universal branch. They do not discuss double descent.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops a replica-based Bayes-optimal theory and evaluates sample-rate sweeps in extensive-width shallow teacher-student networks; it does not report a model-size sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The transition and generalisation behaviour vary with activation function, inner-weight prior, label-noise level, read-out prior, and—in HMC experiments—initialisation.

fits_no_version.finding: Near interpolation (n ≈ kd), the Bayes-optimal error shows a discontinuous drop at a specialisation transition αsp rather than a peak. Reaching the better phase appears exponentially slow in d for ADAM and HMC with discrete read-outs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Near the interpolation threshold, optimal generalisation in wide two-layer networks undergoes a first-order learning transition (universal → specialisation) that practical algorithms may fail to reach.

record.problems: The theory relies on heuristic replica and Gaussian assumptions. Experiments use finite dimensions and small numbers of instances (16 for Figure 1, 9 for Figure 2, and 5 for Figure 8); the Figure 2 error estimate also relies on assumptions stated by the authors. Some experimental settings show non-equilibration or possible computational hardness.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 6 and Figure 9 report training time to reach an error or overlap threshold, not the error curve itself; Figures 3–5 and 10 report overlaps, mutual information, or transition locations rather than the claim's error shape.

untested.parts: No sweep of model size or width; γ is fixed at 0.5.
There are training-loss trajectories (Fig. 8), but only far past interpolation (α = 5), and the text does not describe their shape. Epoch-wise fall-rise-fall is not assessed.
Non-Bayes-optimal learners are not covered: ERM, unregularised or minimum-norm training. The authors list mismatched/ERM settings as future work.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.

Label noise ∆ is varied only for the transition location (Fig. 5 right). There is no comparison of a suboptimal estimator against the optimally regularised one to show a peak disappearing, and no multiple peaks.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label was replaced with 'limits_scope', and all 'reversed' states changed to 'absent'. The study evaluates Bayes-optimal estimators, which are effectively optimally regularised. Monotone error in n is expected there and does not contradict V3, whose sample-wise peak arises for unregularised or minimum-norm learners. The tranche is T3 rather than T2, because the method is not aimed at the double-descent question. Several numerical points use informative initialisation or non-equilibrated samplers, and instance counts are small (16, 9, 5).

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of model size or test error against model size.
Test loss is plotted against gradient updates for ADAM, not epochs; the plotted curves do not have a textual description sufficient to determine whether they show fall-rise-fall.
The study tests sample-rate sweeps in its specified extensive-width teacher-student settings, not other data distributions or architectures.
No capacity sweep across model classes or general risk-versus-capacity curve.
No test of whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.

The paper varies label noise in phase-transition analyses but does not test whether a double-descent peak is noise-driven, splits into multiple peaks, or disappears under optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective parameter measure or test of whether that turns a second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

relationships.condition: Bayes-optimal (posterior-mean) prediction in extensive-width two-layer teacher-student networks, with binary or Gaussian inner weights and several activations, swept across n ≈ kd.
relationships.reason: Theory, posterior sampling and GAMP-RIE all show error falling or flat with α through the interpolation point, with no sample-wise rise (R1–R18). More data does not hurt under Bayes-optimal inference, consistent with the peak requiring suboptimal regularisation.
relationships.display_finding: Theory, posterior sampling, and GAMP-RIE show error decreasing or remaining flat through interpolation, without worsening from additional samples.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Bayes-optimal (posterior-mean) prediction in extensive-width two-layer teacher-student networks, with binary or Gaussian inner weights and several activations, swept across n ≈ kd.
source_check.reason: Falling or flat theoretical error qualifies the learner conditions for existential V3. However, R2/R5/R8 follow an informatively initialised branch, R11/R14 are non-equilibrated, and GAMP-RIE is not globally Bayes-optimal beyond specialisation. These results do not establish that suboptimal regularisation is necessary for a peak.

relation.reason: The study reports its own generalisation-error results as training sample rate varies near interpolation.

tranche.reason: Sample-rate results bear on V3 in a new setting: matched Bayesian teacher-student inference with extensive-width shallow networks.

source_check.notes: Appendix C and the Figure 2 estimator express error above label-noise variance, εopt − Δ; preserve that convention in numerical extractions. Figure 2 uses 10^4 test inputs per instance and assumes Gibbs-error concentration and Nishimori identities.

reader_labels.reason: The text says generalisation error decays with sample rate, and the reported curves show decreases rather than an increase with more data; see R1–R18.
